chunks: It is narrated from Bakkar ibn Abi Bakr, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who has money owed to him by another man,
when the debt becomes due, the debtor says to him, 'Sell me some goods so that I may sell them and repay you what I owe.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as)
key_terms.بَكَّارُ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ: Bakkar ibn Abi Bakr, a narrator
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to settle a debt by buying and immediately selling back goods (inah)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights the permissibility of *Inah* (sale with immediate buyback) as a practical mechanism for debt settlement, reflecting the flexibility of Shia fiqh in commercial transactions. Bakkar ibn Abi Bakr reports that Imam al-Sadiq (as) affirmed its validity, indicating that despite later scholarly debates regarding its potential to mimic riba (usury), it remains a legally sound method for clearing debts when executed with mutual consent.
